submitter: bugfix_277_required_fields_repair lane — bugs_open/083 candidate 2, ROUND 2 (resubmit on corr 05a3d1c8)
rationale:
ROUND 2 on corr 05a3d1c8 (round 1 = REVISE, gated by prior_art_librarian HIGH). Every objection was re-measured 2026-08-17 against the live DB and the running binary — not carried forward from round 1's notes, and one of those notes turned out to be over-broad and is corrected below. The round also carries a defect the council did NOT find: 430's OWN submitted risk 2 has fired, and this round closes it.

WHAT ROUND 1 GOT RIGHT AND THIS ROUND ACTS ON. The pipeline objection (editquality edit 1, guardian edit 1) was sound in premise: pipeline='build' was rewritten unconditionally and 'diagnose' is a live loop with its own gate. It has never fired — but it is now closed by migration 444, as an ALLOW-list rather than the deny-list the objection implied, because the measurement says a deny-list would be the weaker patch (see grounded_in 3). debug_historian's LOW ask for a separate rollback file is met literally: 444 ships with 444_..._ROLLBACK.sql. guardian's LOW ask to confirm the Go diff did not touch the per-pass cap is answered with the diff itself.

THE DEFECT NOBODY OBJECTED TO, WHICH IS THE REAL REASON THIS ROUND EXISTS. 430's submitted risks named it: 'the known-good rule trusts ONE lifetime complete per pair; a pair whose only complete was a false success qualifies.' Of 85 rows promoted since apply, 19 ended failed. Computing each pair's record AS IT STOOD at the instant of its promotion, literal_markdown->page-build-handler was at 1 complete / 28 failed = 3% when the promoter gave it 6 more, 5 of which failed. 444 adds a 25% success floor for pairs with >=5 terminal outcomes, threshold set by a census gap rather than chosen. This is offered as the honest content of a REVISE round: the seats' objections were all answerable, and the change still needed fixing for a reason none of them raised.

A CORRECTION TO ROUND 1'S OWN ANSWER, made here rather than quietly. The note answering bug_historian's reaper objection said 'every enabled reaper pre_query keys on claimed_at'. That is FALSE fleet-wide — thunder-reaper mentions created_at, and stale-orchestration-reaper and stuck-task-reaper key on neither. The narrower claim is the one that actually answers the objection and it holds: of the 10 enabled tasks whose pre_query touches site_work_items, the three that can reap or time out an item all key on claimed_at and none on created_at.

WHY THIS IS STILL SQL AND NOT AN INVOCATION OF THE GO ACTION (reuse_agent, edit 1) — stated, not conceded. TriageDetectedItemsAction is site-scoped and workflow-embedded: driving it needs an orchestration per site per tick, which is a heavier, spawn-bearing mechanism than the transition warrants and re-arms the improvement-loop surface the owner's ruling deliberately left paused. A pre_query that IS the worker (fire_message=false) is the estate's own SCH-006 pattern for exactly this shape, with feasibility-recheck as the exact precedent. The drift risk reuse_agent names is real and is why 430 mirrors the action's UPDATE field-for-field and 444 changes only the SELECT that chooses rows — the transition itself is untouched.

plan.summary: Close two doors on the detected-item-promoter's candidate selection (migration 444, applied and ledger-recorded, with a separate rollback file): a pipeline allow-list answering the council's round-1 objection, and a 25% success floor answering 430's own risk 2, which has fired and cost 5 failed dispatches. 430 is ledger-recorded and is not edited. Record the corrections to bugs_open/083's verify criteria, two of which were measuring the wrong thing.

edits.rationale: Two added predicates and nothing else; every other line is byte-identical to 430's pre_query, which the verify block asserts (a negative control against a copy-paste error: if the rewrite dropped the LIMIT 20 cap, the original_pipeline stamp, the pipeline rewrite, the known-good test or the active-handler test, the promoter would still 'work' and silently misbehave). (1) DOOR 1, the council's objection: AND wi.pipeline IN ('build','content','design'). An ALLOW-list, deliberately not NOT IN ('diagnose','report'): 'report' is not a pipeline value that exists on this table (0 rows) while 'experience' (7) and 'maintenance' (1) are, so the deny-list names one value that cannot fire and misses two that can. pipeline is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'build', so an IN-list has no NULL hole. A new pipeline value is HELD rather than rewritten — the same philosophy as the existing known-good rule. (2) DOOR 2, 430's fired risk 2: a pair with >=5 terminal outcomes must be succeeding at >=25%. The sub-5 exemption means a brand-new pair is still admitted on its first success and held only by the existing rule, so the canary bootstrap is untouched. Both doors hold 0 rows today. The verify block therefore asserts 0-and-0 AND carries a POSITIVE control — literal_markdown->page-build-handler must FAIL the floor — because without it 'holds 0 rows' is equally consistent with a predicate that is simply inert.
edits.sketch:
AND COALESCE(wi.handler_agent, '') <> ''
+          -- DOOR-CLOSER 1: only pipelines this transition has ever produced.
+          AND wi.pipeline IN ('build', 'content', 'design')
           AND EXISTS ( ...active agent_definitions row... )
           AND EXISTS ( ...>=1 lifetime complete for the exact pair... )
+          -- DOOR-CLOSER 2: >=5 terminal outcomes => must still be >=25% good.
+          -- NB `failed` rows have no completed_at, so this keys on status only.
+          AND (
+            SELECT (c + f) < 5 OR c >= 0.25 * (c + f)
+            FROM (
+              SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE h.status = 'complete') AS c,
+                     count(*) FILTER (WHERE h.status = 'failed')   AS f
+              FROM site_work_items h
+              WHERE h.item_type = wi.item_type
+                AND h.handler_agent = wi.handler_agent
+            ) hist
+          )
           ORDER BY wi.created_at ASC
           LIMIT 20

It restores 430's pre_query verbatim as a COPY (430 is ledger-recorded and must not be edited), and its own DO block asserts BOTH directions: neither door-closer may survive the restore, AND 430's five predicates must all be present — so a half-applied rollback that leaves the row neither 430 nor 444 aborts instead of committing. Named symptom in the header for when to use it: the promotable pile stops draining while the task keeps ticking.

DO $$ ... IF q LIKE '%0.25 * (c + f)%' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'door-closer still present'; ... IF q NOT LIKE '%LIMIT 20%' ... THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'neither 430 nor 444'; END $$;

grounded_in: [1] ROUND-1 GATING OBJECTION (prior_art_librarian, HIGH): 'that reads as evidence of at least a second (undescribed) promoter path for detected items'. RE-MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-17, third independent time: SELECT type FROM agent_definitions WHERE is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL AND default_config::text LIKE '%triage_detected_items%' -> exactly ONE row, improvement-loop. SELECT name, enabled, last_triggered_at FROM scheduled_tasks WHERE name='improvement-sweep' -> enabled=FALSE, last fired 2026-08-14 16:34. The doc_notes landmine the seat cites ('two other agents run the same step') PREDATES migration 286, which removed the other two carriers; it is a dated snapshot, not a live count. The premise stands as a fresh query.

[2] SAME OBJECTION, INDEPENDENT SECOND INSTRUMENT: of the 10 ENABLED scheduled tasks whose pre_query touches site_work_items (build-pipeline-trigger, claimed-item-timeout, detected-item-promoter, diagnose-pipeline-trigger, feasibility-recheck, report-dispatch, site-discovery-rotation-availability, site-discovery-rotation-quality, site-render-audit-rotation, stale-work-item-reaper), NONE besides detected-item-promoter writes status='triaged' from 'detected'. A second promoter path would have to be one of these ten or the Go action in [1].

[3] PIPELINE OBJECTION (editquality edit 1 / guardian edit 1, MEDIUM), measured three ways. (a) Lifetime promotions, i.e. every row ever carrying spec.original_pipeline across BOTH implementations, n=1562: build 1055, design 310, content 197. ZERO diagnose, ZERO report — the disconfirming result exists and did not occur. (b) Pipelines that EXIST fleet-wide, all statuses, n=8421: build 7749, content 490, design 130, diagnose 44, experience 7, maintenance 1 — so 'report' is not a value on this table at all, while experience and maintenance are, which is why 444 uses an ALLOW-list: the deny-list the objection implies names one value that cannot fire and misses two that can. (c) diagnose-pipeline-trigger is an ENABLED task, so the seat's premise that diagnose is a live loop with its own gate is correct.

[4] 430's OWN RISK 2, FIRED. Of 85 rows promoted since apply (spec ? 'original_pipeline' AND triaged_at >= 2026-08-15 19:00Z): complete 61, failed 19, needs_human_review 3, wont_fix 2. Counterfactual computing each pair's record AS IT STOOD at its promotion instant: literal_markdown->page-build-handler 1 complete / 28 failed = 3% (6 promoted, 5 failed); audit_tool->tool-auditor 18/21 = 46% (12 promoted, 8 failed); phantom_internal_link->page-build-handler 7/8 = 47% (2 promoted, 2 failed); every other pair >=60%.

[5] THE THRESHOLD IS SET BY A CENSUS, NOT CHOSEN. Success ratios of all 28 (item_type, handler_agent) pairs holding >=1 lifetime complete, ascending: 3, 41, 42, 46, 50, 67, 79, 80, 86, 86, 88, 89, 94, 96, 98, 99, 100 x12. A floor anywhere in 10-35% isolates exactly the one pathological pair and touches nothing else; 25% sits mid-gap. The 41-47% pairs are a SEPARATE question (are those handlers defective?) and are deliberately NOT bundled — named so the silence reads as a decision, per the guardian's standing bundling objection.

[6] 444 APPLIED WITH TWO CONTROLS THAT CAME OUT OPPOSITE WAYS IN ONE RUN. Read-only dry run before apply: promotable_before=0, pipeline_door_holds=0, ratio_door_holds=0; POSITIVE control literal_markdown->page-build-handler (c=1,f=28) -> passes_floor = FALSE (the floor CAN hold something, so the 'holds 0' assert is not vacuous); NEGATIVE control page_rerender->page-rerender (c=4017,f=21) -> passes_floor = TRUE (the floor does not hold everything). At apply the DO block emitted: '444: detected-item-promoter door-closers live. Promotable pile unchanged at 0 (pipeline door held 0, ratio door held 0). Positive control OK'. Ledger: 444 recorded via run-migrations.sh --record-only with a note.

[7] LANDMINE THE FINDING IN [4] NEARLY DIED ON: `failed` rows carry NO completed_at. Control run in the same breath: SELECT status, count(*), count(completed_at) FROM site_work_items WHERE status IN ('failed','complete') GROUP BY 1 -> failed 265 rows / 0 with completed_at; complete 5921 / 5882. The first counterfactual keyed on completed_at and returned 100% success for ALL 17 pairs — a clean, plausible, uniformly-excellent table in which the disconfirming result was unreachable. Re-keyed on updated_at it produced [4]. Now in LANDMINES.md (synced + verifier dispatched, corr a7f078d0) and WRONG_CALLS.md.

[8] CORRECTION TO ROUND 1's OWN REAPER ANSWER (bug_historian edit 1, MEDIUM). Round 1's note claimed 'every enabled reaper pre_query keys on claimed_at' — FALSE fleet-wide: thunder-reaper mentions created_at; stale-orchestration-reaper and stuck-task-reaper key on neither. The claim that actually answers the objection is narrower and holds: of the enabled tasks whose pre_query touches site_work_items, the three that can reap or time out an item — claimed-item-timeout, stale-work-item-reaper, report-dispatch — ALL key on claimed_at and NONE on created_at. A row promoted from 'detected' has no claimed_at until the dispatcher claims it, so promotion cannot expose it to any of the three.

[9] SIBLING BORN-TRIAGED PRODUCERS (editquality edit 2 LOW / bug_historian edit 2 MEDIUM: 'a census of discovery_checks/* for other Status:"triaged" writers before calling the revert complete'). Census run: grep -rn 'Status:\s*"triaged"' --include=*.go platform/ internal/ (excluding _test.go) -> exactly 3 lines in 2 files: check_integrity.go:141, :165 and check_tool_acceptance_due.go:134 (whose own comment reads 'no human judgment needed; triage may not sweep'). Positive control for the grep: 43 files write Status:"detected". Both pairs are known-good, so the promoter would carry them if their lanes revert; that is their lanes' call and is NOT bundled here.

[10] GUARDIAN edit 2 (LOW): 'confirm the diff doesn't touch the per-pass cap / early-return logic'. Answered with the diff: git show --stat 3c6354059 -- check_required_fields_missing.go = 1 file changed, 8 insertions, 5 deletions; the entire change is one WorkItemSpec field (Status: "triaged" -> "detected") plus its comment block. Nothing in or near the loop or the early return.

[11] DEBUG_HISTORIAN edit 2 (MEDIUM): 'the plan names no pod-grep verification step'. Superseded by a stronger instrument and executed: chassis v1.0.1305, OCI label org.opencontainers.image.revision = 6a782274b, confirmed at the running binary with both controls in one exec (label sha PRESENT in /proc/1/exe; live HEAD 896c5aeeb, a real but different commit, ABSENT). git merge-base --is-ancestor 3c6354059 6a782274b exits 0, so the producer revert is live. The startup 'build provenance' log line had already scrolled past --tail=100000 on both pods, which is why the label+binary route was used rather than logs.

[12] BUG 083 VERIFY CRITERION 3 MET, at the SERVED page and not the row status. Four promoted+completed rows on mortgagecalculator.co.uk: /guides/missed-payments/index.html (2009 visible chars), /investor/index.html (2641), /contact/index.html (1426), /guides/index.html (1981) — all HTTP 200 with real on-topic h1s. Second, independent instrument: page.updated_at moved 5-42 SECONDS BEFORE the item's completed_at in all four cases, the causal order real work leaves behind. Method trap recorded: the first fetch of all four returned 404 because the rows store /guides/index.html and the site does not serve the trailing-slash form; the control (site root -> 200, 37KB) is what separated 'the subject is broken' from 'my request is wrong'.

[13] CRITERION 1's METER IS WRONG AND IS RESTATED. Raw count of status='detected' = 82 today (was 4 yesterday), which reads as a stalled promoter. Partition: 77 rows have NO handler_agent (image_url_404 41, head_essentials_missing 36) and can never be promoter candidates — 40 of them were restored to 'detected' DELIBERATELY this morning by the concurrent bugs_closed/284 lane's migration 442; 5 rows have a handler; 0 of those pass the known-good rule. The promotable pile is 0 and the promoter is behaving exactly as designed.

[14] INTERACTION WITH THE CONCURRENT 284 LANE, checked before writing 444 rather than after: migration 443 added CHECK swi_no_handlerless_promotable = NOT (COALESCE(handler_agent,'')='' AND status IN ('triaged','approved','claimed')). This promoter already requires a non-empty handler with a live agent_definitions row, so the constraint is a hard DB-level backstop BEHIND that predicate, not a conflict — a future promoter bug that promoted a handler-less row would now abort the tick loudly instead of misrouting silently.

[15] CRITERION 2 WAS ALREADY MET BEFORE THIS MECHANISM EXISTED, and both prior blocks said otherwise. phantom_internal_link: complete 7, all completed_at between 2026-08-09 15:33 and 2026-08-11 18:44, all carrying original_pipeline — i.e. promoted by the ORIGINAL TriageDetectedItemsAction path, six days before 430 was written. Met on its wording; NOT evidence about candidate 2. Corrected in the bug file, the register entry and WRONG_CALLS rather than banked.
plan.risks:
1) THE FLOOR IS A JUDGEMENT AND THE ONE THING IN THIS ROUND I WOULD MOST LIKE ARGUED WITH. 25% is set by a census gap (3%, then 41%) rather than by theory, so it is well-evidenced for TODAY's population and could need moving as pairs change. Its failure mode is asymmetric and mild: a pair wrongly held stays visible at 'detected' and a human can promote one row by hand (the existing canary path); a pair wrongly admitted burns up to 20 dispatches a tick, which is what just happened. It is also fully reversible by one file — 444_..._ROLLBACK.sql.

2) THE FLOOR MEASURES THE PAIR, NOT THE CAUSE. literal_markdown->page-build-handler may be failing for a reason that has nothing to do with the pair (a site, a template, a transient). Holding it is the right conservative act for the PROMOTER, but it is not a diagnosis, and if the underlying handler bug is fixed the pair stays held until its ratio recovers — which, at 1/28, needs about 9 successes. Named, not solved: 'is page-build-handler defective for these types?' is a separate bug and is deliberately not bundled.

3) 'HOLDS 0 ROWS TODAY' IS THE WEAKEST KIND OF EVIDENCE and I have tried to say so honestly rather than present it as a clean bill of health. It is exactly what an inert predicate also produces. The positive control in the verify block is the answer to that objection, not the 0 itself.

4) THE ALLOW-LIST WILL NEED MAINTAINING. A genuinely new pipeline value that SHOULD be promotable will be silently held until someone adds it. That is the deliberate trade (hold the unknown rather than reroute it), it matches the known-good rule's philosophy, and a held row is visible where a misrouted one is not — but it is a maintenance burden and a future reader should know it was chosen, not overlooked.

5) THE PROMOTER STILL TRUSTS 'complete'. 016b's standing warning is that complete is not proof the work happened, so a pair could hold a high ratio on hollow successes. 083's criterion 3 (verify at the live page) is the intended check and was run for the first time this round on 4 rows — a sample, not a sweep.
